messages.content:
Three ants walk on a thin rod 100 cm long.
When an ant reaches either end of the rod it falls off. When two ants meet,
they BOUNCE: both instantly reverse direction, and each keeps its own speed.

Starting positions and velocities (positive = toward the 100 cm end):

- Ant A: at 10 cm, moving +3 cm/s
- Ant B: at 40 cm, moving -1 cm/s
- Ant C: at 80 cm, moving -2 cm/s

After how many seconds does the LAST ant fall off the rod? Give the exact
number of seconds.


When you are finished, output your final answer on its own line, as the last line of your response, in the exact format:
ANSWER: <your answer>

text:
The collisions can be simulated directly by computing successive meeting times (only three ants are present, so the sequence of events is short and unambiguous).

- Ants A and B move toward each other and collide after \(30/4=7.5\) s at position \(32.5\). Their velocities become \(-3\) and \(+1\), respectively. Ant C has not yet met anyone.
- Ant A now travels left a distance \(32.5\) at speed \(3\) and reaches the left end at time \(7.5+32.5/3=55/3\), falling off. Simultaneously, ants B and C (now approaching each other) collide at position \(130/3\).
- After this second collision the velocities of B and C become \(-1\) and \(+2\). They are moving away from each other, so no further meetings occur.
- Ant C then travels right a distance \(170/3\) at speed \(2\) and falls off the right end at time \(55/3+85/3=140/3\).
- Ant B travels left a distance \(130/3\) at speed \(1\) and falls off the left end at time \(55/3+130/3=185/3\).

The three fall-off times are therefore \(55/3\), \(140/3\) and \(185/3\). The last of them is \(185/3\).

ANSWER: 185/3
